A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Online Language Splatting and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. All 23 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2 support comparison, including relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Replica and TUM RGB-D experiments, localization and rendering measurements, runtime evaluations, and component ablations, with additional empirical results in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds compression comparisons, a cross-view consistency result, and a runtime result using Hi-SLAM.

M1.justification: The SRD, two-stage 768-to-32-to-15 compression, disentangled Gaussian optimization, losses, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Hi-SLAM appears as an additional timed configuration without a newly specified language-mapping component or algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: Replica, TUM RGB-D, COCO, and Omnidata coverage is retained, including the existing open-vocabulary tests. The added compression analysis uses already evaluated Replica scenes; no new dataset, population, or input-environment condition is documented.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 adds a comparison without the generalized encoder in the new cross-view consistency ablation. External baseline membership remains unchanged. Single-stage compression was already evaluated in v1, so its appearance in v2 Table 14 does not itself establish a new baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds a Hi-SLAM configuration for runtime evaluation and evaluates encoder removal through cross-view cosine similarity. Retained benchmark splits, resolutions, and training budgets are unchanged. These are additional evaluation configurations, rather than demonstrated reruns of the existing comparisons.

E4.justification: v2 supplements the existing SRD, OLAE, code-size, and disentanglement studies with a generalized-encoder cross-view consistency ablation and further single-stage versus two-stage compression results in Section 12.2/Table 14. The earlier analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same population-mean-plus-two-standard-deviations failure cutoff in Section 14/Table 13, and leave uncertainty quantification to future work.

E6.justification: Table 7 revises LangSplat scores in six scenes: Room1 mIoU/Loc changes from 0.459/0.779 to 0.393/0.718, while Table 1's summary remains unchanged. New Table 14 reports single-stage/two-stage means of 0.434/0.808 and 0.501/0.835. v2 also reports cosine similarity of 0.5 without the generalized encoder and 7.05 FPS with Hi-SLAM. Network time changes from 23 to 21 ms despite retaining the 15+2+6 ms breakdown.

T1.justification: The Gaussian rendering and gradient equations, SRD loss definitions, and supplementary disentanglement mathematics are retained. The new cross-view discussion provides an interpretation, not a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about online open-vocabulary mapping, the three principal components, accuracy, and over 40-fold efficiency gains. The added experiments do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting the generalized encoder and Gaussian mapping to cross-view consistency, and discusses accuracy versus memory and complexity for staged compression. Tracking relative to MonoGS is reinterpreted from a slight improvement to parity. Existing static-scene and small-object limitations remain.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section 7 adds information about generating SRD supervision through SAM masks, point sampling, clustering, and refinement. Section 5 newly states that post-stage global refinement is excluded; v1 does not establish the opposite setting. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 newly names Hi-SLAM as a framework supporting faster integration, although its citation remains unresolved. The established related-work discussion, bibliography, and principal novelty positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: There are localized additions and rewrites concerning runtime, cross-view consistency, and SRD supervision. Supplementary Section 12 becomes Language Compression, retaining the code-size discussion as Section 12.1 and adding Section 12.2. The overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces LangSplat feature-map panels, and v2 adds compression Table 14. The original category-wise Table 14 is retained as Table 16; other displays, including Figure 7 and Table 8, are relocated. Remaining supplementary visualizations are preserved.

improvement.justification: The additional compression and cross-view analyses and supervision details offer useful support. However, v2 introduces numerical inconsistencies: revised LangSplat scene scores in Table 7 no longer reconcile with the retained Table 1 summary, and the reported 21 ms network time conflicts with components totaling 23 ms. The new Hi-SLAM and cross-view results also lack sufficient evaluation detail. These benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net effect on paper quality uncertain.
